questions.question: Why do finite series not involve convergence issues?

Only finitely many terms are added.
The index set is always unbounded.

Finite sums can equal many values, not always $1$; e.g. $\sum_{i=1}^5 i=15$ and $\sum_{i=1}^3 2^i=14$.
